_meta.indication: Treatment of patients 1 year of age and older with late-onset Pompe disease (lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase [GAA] deficiency).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blinded, multinational, multicenter, active-controlled trial comparing NEXVIAZYME to alglucosidase alfa; patients randomized 1:1 (stratified by baseline FVC, gender, age, and country) to 20 mg/kg every other week for 49 weeks, followed by an open-label long-term follow-up phase.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive patients with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD); enrolled patients were 16 to 78 years of age (median baseline age 49 years).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change in FVC (% predicted) in the upright position from baseline to Week 49.
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean change in FVC (% predicted) at Week 49 was 2.9% (NEXVIAZYME) vs 0.5% (alglucosidase alfa); estimated treatment difference 2.4% (95% CI: -0.1, 5.0) favoring NEXVIAZYME, meeting pre-established noninferiority but not superiority. Key secondary endpoint 6MWT treatment difference was 30 meters (95% CI: 1.3 to 58.7).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis) and infusion-associated reactions. In Study 1 the most frequent AEs in NEXVIAZYME-treated patients (>5%) included headache (22%), fatigue (18%), diarrhea (12%), and nausea (12%); IARs occurred in 25% of NEXVIAZYME patients. Across the pooled safety population serious adverse events occurred in 25% (35/138) of patients.
target_moa: Avalglucosidase alfa is a modified recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) enzyme replacement therapy manufactured by conjugating bis-mannose-6-phosphate (M6P) to alglucosidase alfa (~15-fold increase in M6P moieties) to improve cellular uptake; it provides an exogenous source of GAA to degrade accumulated lysosomal glycogen.
modality: Enzyme (recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase enzyme replacement therapy)

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for severe hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis), infusion-associated reactions, and risk of acute cardiorespiratory failure in susceptible patients. Patients have experienced life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis; discontinue immediately and initiate appropriate treatment if a severe reaction occurs.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise significant public health questions requiring referral.

summary.text: Nexviazyme was granted Orphan Drug designation (Nov 2013), Fast Track designation (Aug 2019), and Breakthrough Therapy designation (June 2020), and the BLA received priority review as a clinically significant improvement in treatment of a serious condition. It was a traditional (non-accelerated) approval based on the phase 3 pivotal trial EFC14028 (COMET).

citations.quote: In November 2013, avalglucosidase alfa was granted an Orphan Drug designation, followed by a Fast Track designation in August 2019, and a Breakthrough Therapy designation in June 2020.

The application met the criteria for a priority review because avalglucosidase alfa would provide a clinically significant improvement in the effectiveness of the treatment for PD, a serious condition.

The pivotal trial, EFC14028, was a randomized, double-blind, comparator-controlled trial in treatment-naïve patients 3 years of age and older with LOPD, comparing avalglucosidase alfa to alglucosidase alfa.

requirement.text: 4026-1: Conduct a worldwide descriptive safety study collecting data in women and their offspring exposed to Nexviazyme during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess pregnancy/maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant; outcomes assessed through at least the first year of life, collecting information for 10 years.

citations.quote: 4026-1 Conduct a worldwide, descriptive safety study that collects data in women and their offspring who are exposed to Nexviazyme (avalglucosidase alfa-ngpt) during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Outcomes of exposed infants,
including growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The study will collect information for 10 years.
